related_debugger_sample.trace_normalization: Trailing whitespace was removed from the committed copy; the final debugger transport-disconnect line is retained.
separate_run_observations: Original UI readiness method returned AL=1 in all eight captured calls.
Native D3DXCreateEffect returned HRESULT 0 for the embedded retail effect.
The retail main thread was in Wine d3d9.dll with a SHIFT.exe caller stack.
related_debugger_sample.debugger_limit: The debugger stopped on a Wine helper/preloader thread outside SHIFT.exe; this is not classified as a retail fault.

interpretation: The original retail executable reached an active race with a visible cockpit HUD and later displayed its main menu on this isolated Wine run. This confirms original-game frontend and race scenes, not P-code gameplay, native Windows behavior, or renderer parity.
limitations: Observed under Wine 11.17, not native Windows.
The native 32-bit D3DX link was repaired only inside the isolated game-root copy; the primary game files and Wine prefix were not changed by that repair.
The user-driven key sequence was not recorded, and the race and main-menu screenshots are separate captures rather than a continuous video.
The active race scene is original-executable evidence and is separate from the recompiled P-code frame-loop replay.
The captured desktop image includes host desktop areas around the game window.
